blocks.text: Jeremiah 41 belongs to the book’s larger account of Judah under Babylonian domination: deportation, Jerusalem’s destruction, Gedaliah’s role, and the later movement toward Egypt. The chapter’s violence and fear therefore appear within a continuing account of a shattered community rather than as an isolated episode. The book itself brings together varied forms of material—poetry, sermons, narratives, letters, headings, repeated accounts, restoration collections, oracles concerning nations, and an appendix—through a long and debated compositional history.
